semantic_distinctions.distinction: Ruby is the language; Rails is the framework written in Ruby.
MVC model is architectural role; Active Record supplies ORM behavior.
Controller is component; action is a response unit within controller.
Route maps an external request to an action; action does not itself define public reachability.
ERB is a template engine; Rails is the application framework.
Rails is framework; Rack is web-server interface.
Rails commonly sits behind a front-end server rather than directly on Internet.
Hotwire is client/web interaction family integrated as Rails 7 default.
Older Rails plugins were deprecated in favor of standard gems.
Scaling depends on broader system architecture, not only framework.
Framework security mechanisms coexist with application/configuration vulnerabilities.

misconceptions.claim: Every Rails request is directly handled by Rails from the Internet
misconceptions.correction: Rails commonly sits behind a front-end web server.

misconceptions.claim: MVC model is identical to Active Record
misconceptions.correction: Active Record is the ORM implementation used for model/database behavior.

misconceptions.claim: A controller action is automatically public
misconceptions.correction: A route must map an external request to the controller action.

misconceptions.claim: Rails scaling is only a framework problem
misconceptions.correction: Source emphasizes database, cache, server and architecture choices.
Rails 7 made import maps the default and moved away from Webpack as default.
Rails 7 replaced Turbolinks with Turbo + Stimulus.

misconceptions.claim: Rails extensions are primarily custom plugins
misconceptions.correction: Rails 3.2 deprecated custom plugin framework in favor of gems.

misconceptions.claim: Ruby and Rails are interchangeable names
misconceptions.correction: Ruby is the language; Rails is written in Ruby.
Source documents encryption, CSP, security work and security vulnerabilities.
